To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the components of KOI-126 have radii and surface temperature consistent with their masses; (2) CM Draconis cannot be modelled with the currently estimated metallicities, but the discrepancy is reduced if α is lowered; (3) a higher metallicity can account for the radius discrepancy, and (4) a higher metal content and lower α can explain the observations of both systems.

the models of the components in the systems KOI 126 and CM Dra are consistent with the observations for the system KOI 126, and that the models of CM Dra are not consistent with the observed radiative fluxes and temperatures, unless the metallicity of this system is significantly increased.

the models are consistent with the system KOI 126, and that the discrepancy between the models and the observations of the system CM Draconis can be explained by a combination of a high metallicity and a low value of α.
